research_method: Source-preserving, additive extraction. Regional flora pages are printed page numbers. Explicitly distinguish FNA genus/key vs full species accounts and note source-access gaps.

records.source: FNA vol.19 species account and genus account

morphology.habit: Introduced Eurasian taprooted perennial with rush-like, stiff, much-branched stems, ca. 40–150 cm (genus)
morphology.stems: Coarsely bristly at base, upper flowering stems nearly glabrous
morphology.leaves: Basal rosette blades 5–13 × 1.5–3 cm, runcinate-pinnatifid, often withered when flowering; upper stem leaves reduced, linear
morphology.heads: Many solitary or grouped axillary/terminal ligulate heads, about 7–15 yellow florets per head (genus)
morphology.involucres: Genus cylindrical, 2.5–5 mm diameter, 5–9 major phyllaries
morphology.fruits: Beaked cylindrical ribbed cypsela, about 3–4 mm body, a white bristle pappus; source descriptions vary in whether beak counted

flags: Source genus measurements tagged rather than asserted as exclusive species measurements.
FNA full species page was intermittently unavailable, so phenology excluded.

records.source: FNA vol.21 Chromolaena genus and identification key; existing species record for supplementary details

morphology.habit: Perennial or subshrub; flowering growth often erect to sprawling (genus)
morphology.leaves: Opposite, petioles 5–20 mm; large blades mostly (3.5–)5–10 cm, generally deltate to ovate-lanceolate with toothed margins and 3 basal veins
morphology.heads: Disk-only heads in groups of 5–50+ in corymbiform clusters
morphology.involucres: Cylindric, usually (7–)8–10 mm in the FNA key; phyllaries many imbricate in ≥4 series (genus)
morphology.flowers: Tubular disk florets whitish, pinkish, pale purple; no rays
morphology.fruits: Genus prismatic (3–)5-ribbed cypsela, scabrellous, ~40 barbellate pappus bristles

flags: FNA genus and key verified; narrower species-specific metrics are from the established species record and require separate citation.
No regional Diggs species treatment established.

records.source: FNA vol.21 Chrysactinia (monotypic in U.S. flora) genus account

morphology.habit: Evergreen aromatic subshrub/shrub, usually 10–40 cm (occasionally taller)
morphology.leaves: Alternate narrow entire blades, linear to club-shaped or needlelike, conspicuous marginal/submarginal oil glands
morphology.heads: Single yellow radiate heads on branches; no calyculus
morphology.involucres: Turbinate/hemispheric ~3.5–5 mm across, 8–14 carinate phyllaries in ca. 2 series, each with 1–5 oil glands
morphology.receptacle: Convex to hemispheric, pitted, usually naked
morphology.fruits: Cylindrical to spindle-shaped cypselae; ~30–40 persistent pappus bristles

flags: Numbers are genus-level FNA characters; genus has only one member in the FNA flora, not necessarily global genus-exclusive.

records.source: FNA vol.21 Conoclinium genus key; UT Austin Wildflower Center synonym crosswalk

morphology.leaves: Opposite, petiolate; blades deeply lobed or dissected with toothed lobes, unlike entire-to-dentate C. coelestinum
morphology.heads: Conical naked receptacle, disk-only corymbiform clusters; tubular blue-violet florets
morphology.involucres: Genus hemispherical, 3–6 mm diameter; about 25 phyllaries in 2–3 series
morphology.florets: Genus 35–70+ per head, no ray florets

flags: Genus-level measurements separated from species-level leaf character.
UT Austin and POWO support Conoclinium greggii as historical synonym; 1999 regional account not found.

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999) comparative note under Coreopsis wrightii

morphology.habit: Annual, per Coreopsis basalis/wrightii key grouping; independent life-cycle account still to confirm
morphology.leaves: Middle/upper leaves broadly segmented; terminal leaflet on middle leaf generally <3 times as long as broad and about 5–15 mm wide
morphology.heads: Genus ca. 8 sterile yellow rays and brownish-red disk corollas in the C. basalis/wrightii group
morphology.phyllaries: Genus inner phyllaries fused basally into cup; outer distinct
morphology.fruits: Flattened cypsela with 2 awns varying across genus

flags: Flora account is comparative and explicitly says distribution just east/south of north-central-Texas study region.
Do not assign C. wrightii's narrower 1–3 mm terminal leaflets to basalis.
Species-level fruit and dimensions beyond comparative note withheld.

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999) full species account + genus key

morphology.habit: Perennial 0.3–0.7 m, foliage crowded on lower stem with flowering peduncles commonly >15 cm
morphology.leaves: Usually simple or with 1–2 lobes, divisions 5–30 mm wide; distal stems largely leafless
morphology.heads: Radiate yellow flowerheads, about 8 rays per genus; ligules 15–30 mm, 4–5 toothed
morphology.phyllaries: Outer lanceolate phyllaries shorter than/equal inner, 5–10 mm
morphology.fruits: Flat thin-winged achenes; 2 awns or reduced pappus per genus

flags: Regional account concerns its 1999 area and introduction along highways; do not infer current BONAP local nativity.

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999) full species account + genus key

morphology.leaves: Opposite per genus; pinnately compound, lower terminal leaflets linear, upper divisions becoming threadlike
morphology.heads: Yellow ligules with brown/red basal marks, 10–15 mm long; disk corollas reddish-brown above
morphology.phyllaries: Outer phyllaries much shorter than inner, around 2 mm, linear-oblong to triangular
morphology.florets: Ray ligules bluntly 3-toothed; disk corollas 4-lobed with 4 anthers (key)
morphology.habitat: Low moist often sandy places, cultivated as ornamental

flags: Compare C. wrightii: 5-lobed disk corollas, 5 anthers, and outer phyllaries longer.

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999) full species account + genus key

morphology.leaves: Pinnately compound, middle/upper leaflets narrow; middle terminal leaflet >3× long as wide, only 1–3 mm wide
morphology.heads: Yellow ligules usually brown-red at base, 4–5-toothed; reddish-brown disk corollas
morphology.phyllaries: Outer linear phyllaries about 4–11 mm, equal to or longer than inner
morphology.fruits: Cypselae wingless, pappus of 2 awns sometimes reduced per genus

flags: Do not merge historical Coreopsis basalis var. wrightii with modern Coreopsis basalis; this variety is synonym of C. wrightii in 1999 treatment.
